P1.evidence: P1b is three parts of four — 'I just want to understand, like, what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're actually trying to get with your fitness and health in general' — with nothing on what he needs. P1c ran and was answered: 'Sounds good?' — 'That's good.' P1d immediately followed: 'walk me through. What's been going on? What's the main thing that brought you here, actually?' P1a is not applicable; there is no setter on this inbound call. Worth noting for a separate reason that the rep introduced himself as 'a senior advisor here with Trevor's team, so you're in good hands' before collecting medical and financial history.

P2.evidence: P2d is the standout and the best injury work in the batch — 'Anything connected with a long time sitting in the meetings? Like any back pains', then 'Tell me more about what happened', then 'So any other injuries or anything that may limit your movement?', then a functional follow-up on whether the knee shows up day to day and under load, and he established the duration at nearly ten years. P2b is a full hit including the desk question and a steps check. P2a is partial under the volunteered rule: age was asked ('may I ask how old are you?') but height and weight came out unprompted inside a goals answer — 'I'm 250 pounds at 6'4"' — and were never requested. P2c is partial: 'any other maybe chronic conditions whatsoever?' ran, hereditary history did not. P2f is partial because 'every time I go to the gym, it seems like I kind of add bulk up' was volunteered, though the rep did probe it. P2i is a miss — energy through the day was never asked, which matters for a man at 3,000 steps a day with monthly long-haul travel.

P3.evidence: P3d ran hard and repeatedly — 'what's the biggest reason you actually want to make this change in your life', 'what sparked this thought?' — and the rep pushed back properly when the prospect deflected with 'You had to have a, like, at least a thought, like, yeah?' P3c is a hit via 'do you have like any sports goals?' followed by 'Would you like to get back to it?', which surfaced that he has not jumped in a decade. P3h is a clean reflect-back that got confirmation: 'you're just looking beforehand so you can age gracefully, and you don't have to be dependent on anyone else... Is that correct, or did I miss something?' — 'Nope, that's about it.' P3e ran as the magic-wand question and returned nothing: 'I don't know. I never really thought about that.' The rep accepted that and moved on. P3f is the decisive miss of this call — 'who else does that impact?' was never asked, and as a direct result the rep did not learn the prospect was getting married until it surfaced twenty minutes later as a financial objection. A fiancée is the single strongest available why on this call and it was never used, because nobody asked. P3g is partial: the depth that exists came from the prospect unprompted, the coffin and wheelchair imagery, and the rep followed it well ('You expand a little bit') but did not drive it anywhere further.

P4.evidence: The phase effectively did not run. There is no 'what have you tried before', no 'what happened with that', no 'why do you feel it didn't stick', and the prospect never named a gap. The rep went from the goals reflect-back at 00:21:52 straight into the pillar pitch at 00:22:30. P4d is partial only because 'what's coming up actually for you that's preventing you from getting started?' was asked twice, but both times after the price, so it functioned as objection handling rather than root-cause work. This is the reason the call had no leverage later: with no past-attempt narrative and no named structural gap, there was nothing to return to when $6,000 landed.

P5.evidence: Skipped entirely, the fourth call in this batch where that is true. The striking part is that the prospect did the phase's work himself and the rep did not build on it — 'let's say you're aging, right? And you have a body that's failing you, and you could have made some changes in your life to make that not the case' and 'you're at a wheelchair, and someone's got to take you around everywhere, and you're just, your freedom is gone.' That is the two-year picture, volunteered. No 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The gap question at 00:17:38, 'how far off do you feel like from that you are right now?', got 'probably a fair bit away, I think. I don't know' and was not pursued.

P6.evidence: P6a was asked properly — 'if you had, like, right training, simple nutrition, and this kind of accountability all built around your life, do you agree that that would get you to your aging gracefully goal?' — and returned a refusal to commit: 'I hope so. I don't know what else will... I can't really give you a solid yes or no.' Scored partial because it was asked well and not achieved. P6b is a hit and the rep deserves credit for pressing rather than glossing: 'Are you fully committed to actually showing up and doing the work?... Is that a 100% sure? It doesn't sound like that', followed by a genuine takeaway, 'if you already feel that I will probably fall off after the first month, it doesn't make sense to actually go for it then.' P6c is the pivotal miss. The prospect then told him plainly that his agreement means nothing — 'I'm pretty timid. So I don't really know what to say half the time. So I just kind of throw in words' — and the rep pushed on to a yes anyway, including asking whether it was loud enough, and treated it as the gate cleared. The script says do not move forward without a clear YES and, where hesitation surfaces, return to Phase 5. Phase 5 had never been run, so there was nowhere to return to.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted at two price points so the phase applies and none of it ran. No payment, no link, no Trevor onboarding scheduled, no agreement, no welcome sequence. No contact details were exchanged and no follow-up was booked, so unlike every other unclosed call in this batch there is no path back to this prospect.

objection_plays.detail: The most faithful execution of the money play in this batch — eight of ten moves, several near-verbatim. Isolate ran twice: 'Like finances aside, do you still think that you're 100%, you want to commit and make this change for you?' and 'is there anything else keeping you from being a hundred percent in now?', landing on 'So it's only logistical part of, of the equation, just the finance financing side.' The upfront-versus-break-it-up move ran verbatim and was converted into the explore question: 'for certain clients, I don't feel that's the best thing. Based on their situation, so we break it up. So let me ask you, do you want to explore ways we could potentially make this work?' — 'Yes.' Permission ran verbatim: 'are you comfortable having an open and honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially right now?' — 'Sure.' Then the financial picture, which no other call in this batch actually obtained: cash on hand ($2,000), monthly surplus after bills (~$3,000), credit cards (held, high available credit, unwilling to carry balances), and investments ('all my money is basically tied into my company'). Only 'how many credit cards' and 'used versus available' went unasked. What follows is the coaching point and it is the largest single one in this batch: having established that $2,000 today plus roughly two months of surplus clears $6,000, he proposed no schedule at all and offered a cheaper, shorter product instead. The play's entire purpose is to convert that picture into a structure, and the structure was never built.

Triggered by 'I have to think about it, to be honest with you' and later 'I have to think about it, my friend.' The core diagnostic move ran, twice and well: 'what's coming up actually for you that's preventing you from getting started?' It is what produced the honest final answer. Nothing else ran — no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now'. The first OA move, 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', had already been asked at the commitment check and had returned a hedge, so there was no established belief to anchor the play to.

Triggered clearly by the wedding — 'I'm trying to get married, but yeah, so I have a lot of expenses coming up' — and by the travel calendar. No scripted move ran. The rep improvised a single aesthetic reframe, 'Wouldn't it be like a crazy idea to, when you're getting married, to actually look lean and mean?', which was conceded and dismissed. The obvious play was sitting in the transcript unused: the prospect had said his schedule will not ease 'in the next 10 years' and had just listed four conference trips in six weeks, which is precisely the 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time' setup.

Doubt was present and explicit at the commitment check — 'I hope so. I don't know what else will', 'I've never done a program like this', 'I'm pretty timid... I just kind of throw in words'. No OE move ran. There was no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no bridge, no plane, no burned-before, and no 'how will you know if you never actually try', which was the natural response to a man whose stated reservation was that he had never done a programme like this. The rep pushed for a louder yes instead.

SCRIPT GAP — no play exists for a prospect whose price expectation was anchored at roughly half the offer before the call began. 'I was thinking maybe around $3,000 or $4,000, but $6,000 is pretty, $1,000 a month, basically. That's a lot. I mean, that's just, that's more than I would anticipated.' Objection C is built to find money that exists; it has no move for resetting an expectation formed from inbound content that never mentions price. This is the second instance in this batch after Fletcher Koder, who arrived expecting free, and both came through channels with no price pre-frame — one via a setter, one via Instagram.
No spousal objection was raised. Notable that his fiancée appears only as a source of expense and was never explored as a decision-maker or as a why.

notes: This is the call to use when teaching what the financial picture is actually for. He ran Objection C almost perfectly and then discarded the output: $2,000 now plus $3,000 a month clears $6,000 inside two months, and instead of proposing that schedule he cut the product to three months at $4,000, which the prospect also refused. Build the plan from the numbers you just collected. Two upstream causes made the ending near-inevitable. Phase 4 never ran at all, so there was no structural gap to point back at, and Phase 5 never ran either, so when price landed there was nothing pulling in the other direction — a prospect who had described his own wheelchair fear unprompted was never asked whether he was willing to settle for it. And the commitment gate was forced: he was told outright that this prospect's verbal yes is unreliable and proceeded on one anyway.
